Poirot reasons that a Grand Slam is an exciting and high-risk bid that requires the full attention of all players. He deduces that the murder was committed during this specific hand because the players were too focused on the game to look up. He then identifies that **Dr. Roberts** was the dummy (the partner whose hand is played by the partner) during this hand.

Poirot further explains that Dr. Roberts is a player who "overcalls" (bids higher than his hand warrants) and takes risks. The text highlights that Dr. Roberts' play, particularly the unjustified Grand Slam bid, was a deviation or a specific high-risk move that drew attention and provided the timing for the murder. While "sudden change" is a general concept, the specific clue Poirot relies on is the **high-risk nature of the bid (Grand Slam)** which kept the other players' attention fixed on the cards, allowing the murder to occur unseen.
